author: Mark Atwood
text:
Two paths from the bead body. Both have visible downsides; this needs an explicit decision.

Option (a) rustdoc-only warning on MemoryBackend::query_objects + query_changes
  Pros: minimal cost, no behavior change, no test churn.
  Cons: workspace-canonical 'silent-drop is a bug' rule (cf. JMAP-wlip.1 workspace pattern: 'silent-truncation/silent-drop in any function that mutates state is a data-integrity bug class') is documented but not enforced. The bead's stated worry — consumers copy the silent-ignore shape — is mitigated only by rustdoc visibility.

Option (b) fail-loud: return unsupportedSort / unsupportedFilter SetError when caller specifies non-trivial sort/filter
  Pros: aligned with workspace silent-drop rule. Models correct production behavior in the reference impl.
  Cons: changes behavior. Existing tests in tests/tasks_tests.rs that exercise Task/query may need adjustment if any pass a non-trivial sort/filter today. Demo backend becomes less useful for end-to-end smoke tests.

Option (c) minimal correct: implement filter (taskListId already partial) + sort by id/created/updated/due, only fail-loud on truly unsupported keys.
  Pros: closest to a production-shaped reference impl.
  Cons: most code. Re-derived from the type's QueryObject impl which makes the demo backend dependent on the wire-format property names.

Recommendation: option (a) for query_changes (the comment on the bead is correct that the spec mandate is property-mutability-aware, which the demo can't implement faithfully without re-deriving the type's filter algebra) PLUS option (b) for query_objects with a narrow carve-out: keep the existing inTaskList path for Task (used by the TaskList/set destroy cascade — a real internal use), and fail-loud for everything else. This matches the workspace 'silent-drop is a bug' rule for the surface area the reference impl actually models, while preserving the one filter the kit uses internally.

Cross-reference: JMAP-h47t.4 (just closed in 3e33cf8) shows the alternative shape — the reference MemoryBackend now actively enforces isDraft per the workspace 'backend-canonical' rule. Same logic applies here: the demo should model correct production behavior, not the silent-skip foot-gun. But query is a bigger surface than isDraft and the trade-off matrix is broader, hence the human escalation.
